name: Nota
comment: Conservative 'never lie' TextMate grammar for Nota (contract D1). This grammar is ONLY the honest FIRST PAINT shown for the ~100-500ms before the reader-driven LSP semantic tokens arrive (the semantic-tokens provider, backed by the reader's parse, is the faithful layer and owns everything context-sensitive). To make the derailment class structurally impossible, EVERY rule here is either a single-line `match` or a fence `begin`/`end` whose delimiters are anchored to whole lines (or, for verbatim, to a line boundary). NO rule consumes past end-of-line except the line-anchored fences. Constructs that are not line-locally decidable -- [props] interiors, {bodies}, @(expr)/@if heads, markup-valued props, doc-state sugar (<label>/&ref/[^fn]), else/else-if, verbatim re-arm -- are deliberately LEFT UNPAINTED; claiming them would risk lying, and semantic tokens paint them faithfully. A subset-correctness conformance test (tests/conformance.ts) runs this grammar over integration/*.nota and asserts every Nota-scoped token agrees with the reader's highlight() kind at that offset; underpainting always passes, a wrong claim fails.

main.comment: Top-level markup context. Order matters: TextMate picks the earliest-starting match, breaking ties by list order, so escapes precede sigils, line-anchored block constructs precede inline ones, and raw spans (verbatim/code/math) precede the @-forms and emphasis they might otherwise mis-claim inside.

inline.comment: Single-line inline rules, safe to nest inside a heading (which ends at EOL). Every rule here either matches wholly on one line or is a same-line raw span; none can escape its line.

escape.comment: Backslash escapes for the documented set: the reader classifies `\x` (both bytes) as a single escape span. We scope only the known escapable sigils; a backslash before anything else is literal text.
escape.name: constant.character.escape.nota

statement-fence.comment: %%% ... %%% -- a raw JS block delegated to source.ts. Line-anchored fence: the opening and closing %%% must each be alone on their line (the reader scopes the %%% delimiter runs as sigils; the interior is embedded TS).
statement-fence.name: meta.embedded.block.statement.nota

statement-line.comment: A line-leading % (not %%) begins a JS statement: the sigil, then the rest of the line delegated to source.ts. `end: $` keeps it strictly line-local. 50% mid-line is unaffected; \% forces a literal.
statement-line.name: meta.embedded.line.statement.nota

heading.comment: A line opening with 1-6 # then whitespace -> @h{n}. The reader emits a `heading` under-layer over the whole line and a `heading-marker` over the # run; nested emphasis/code/@-forms overlay it. We mirror that: the whole line is markup.heading.nota, the # run is the marker, and inline rules nest (the region ends at EOL, so it stays line-local).
heading.name: markup.heading.nota

list.comment: List-item markers at line start: - / + (bullet or numbered) and N. (explicit ordered). Only the marker is scoped (the reader classifies it list-marker); the rest of the line is ordinary markup handled by the outer context.

prop-line.comment: A block-sugar prop line: a line-leading `| key: value` under an @head: block. The reader scopes the leading `|` as a sigil; the key/value are left to semantic tokens (we do not embed them -- a line-local grammar cannot know it is inside a block-sugar body, so we claim only the marker). Requires whitespace after `|` to avoid catching stray pipes glued to text.

code-fence.comment: ```lang ... ``` fenced code. Line-anchored: the opening run is line-leading and the closing run of the SAME length is alone on its line (\1 backref, anchored ^..$), so it cannot close mid-content or swallow the rest of the document. Language-tagged fences we ship a grammar for embed that source.{lang}; any other tag (or none) stays raw (reader: `code`). The reader scopes the whole opening line as code-delim with the language overlaid as code-lang, and the closing run as code-delim.

math-fence.comment: $$ alone on a line opens/closes a display-math block (line-anchored fence). The reader scopes the $$ delimiters as math-delim and the interior as raw math. Single-line $$...$$ is handled by #math-display-inline instead (this only fires when $$ is alone on its line).
math-fence.name: markup.math.nota

verbatim-fence.comment: Multi-line verbatim: `|{` at end of line opens a raw block that closes at a line-leading `}|` (e.g. @pre|{ ... }|). This is a SUPPRESSION fence -- its only job is to stop the inline rules from firing on the raw interior (where @foo{x} is literal text, not a tag). We scope the `|{`/`}|` delimiters as sigils (the reader agrees) and leave the interior UNPAINTED: the reader classifies plain content as `verbatim` but re-armed `|@head` content as real tags, and a line-local grammar cannot tell them apart, so underpainting the whole interior is the only honest choice. Anchored to line boundaries (begin ends at $, end starts at ^), so it cannot derail the way a free-floating region would.

verbatim-inline.comment: Same-line verbatim `|{ ... }|` (both delimiters on one line, e.g. @code|{ raw }|). Delimiters scoped as sigils; interior left UNPAINTED (same reasoning as the multi-line fence -- the interior may be raw text or re-armed markup, indistinguishable line-locally, so we make no claim on it).

code-inline.comment: `...` inline code (reader: code-delim + raw code). Single-line only: a run of 1+ backticks, its content (no inner backtick), and a closing run of the same length via \1. If it does not close on the same line, nothing matches (unpainted).

math-display-inline.comment: Single-line display math $$...$$ (reader: math-delim + raw math, interpolations NOT broken out). Tried before inline $ so $$ is never read as two empty $...$.

math-inline.comment: Single-line inline math $...$ (reader: math-delim + raw math). Content is any non-$, non-newline run; if there is no closing $ on the line, nothing matches (unpainted).

control.comment: Content control-flow keyword head @if / @for, recognised only when followed by a `(` condition/iterator (the reader scopes @ as a sigil and if/for as a control keyword). The `(...)` head itself is embedded JS but NOT line-anchored, so we do not enter it -- it is left to semantic tokens. `else`/`else if` are contextual continuations (only meaningful after a matching @if body) and are NOT claimed here.

colon-element.comment: Line-leading colon-sugar element head `@head: body`. Colon sugar only fires at a line-leading position (mid-line `@user:` is a bare interpolation followed by a literal colon), so this rule is anchored to line start; the colon is scoped as a sigil, the body (rest of line) is ordinary markup. Capitalised -> component, lowercase -> host. (A props-then-colon form `@head[..]:` is left to semantic tokens -- the props break the line-local pattern.)

element.comment: Element head `@head` immediately followed by an element trigger `{`, `[`, or `|{` (glued, same line) -- these are unambiguously tags regardless of position. The trigger is a lookahead: the [props]/{body}/verbatim that follow are NOT entered (a line-local grammar cannot balance them, and markup-valued props would derail it). Capitalised -> component, lowercase -> host; the reader agrees on the case split and the sigil.

at-sigil.comment: Bare @( (dynamic tag / parenthesised expression) or @{ (fragment body): the reader scopes only the @ as a sigil and leaves the (...)/{...} to its embedded/markup contents, which we do not enter. We claim just the @.

interpolation.comment: Bare @name identifier interpolation -> {name} (the reader scopes @ as a sigil and the JS-identifier name as interpolation). This fires when @ is followed by an identifier but no element trigger (the tag/control/colon rules run first and consume those cases). The name is a JS IdentifierName (no hyphen), matching the reader, so @my-tag with no trigger yields interpolation `my` and leaves `-tag` literal.

emphasis-strong.comment: *...* -> markup.bold (@strong). Single-line only. Word-boundary guards (fixed-width lookarounds, the closest a regex gets to the reader's rule) keep intra-word * literal: opens only when the * is NOT preceded by a letter/digit and is followed by a non-space/non-*, closes only when the * is NOT followed by a letter/digit -- so `2*3*4` and `a*b*c` stay plain, while `*bold*` (and a whole `*bold _italic_ within*` run) is claimed. Content may not contain a bare * (nested emphasis is left to semantic tokens). If it does not close on the same line, nothing matches.
emphasis-strong.name: markup.bold.nota

emphasis-em.comment: _..._ -> markup.italic (@em). Same word-boundary rule as #emphasis-strong, so my_var_name and snake_case stay literal.
emphasis-em.name: markup.italic.nota
